title: Binding
description: The third artefact. A prose specification decides, an interface model declares, and neither one says which of the model's addresses the document's own inputs and outputs are. Until this file exists that correspondence lives only in somebody's head, and every conversion re-derives it.

document.description: Path to the SCXML this binds, relative to the binding file.

input.x-sce-deliberately-absent: There is no form for comparing SEVERAL addresses at once, and that is a measured decision rather than an oversight. One platform's own rule format has two such keys; measured 2026-09-20 across 499 files of a real corpus, they appear 4 times each, both in ONE of 28 hand-written bindings, against 490 uses of the one-address form in 106 files. The component that binding is for reaches a full pass without the shape when its binding is written in this vocabulary instead, so what the multi-address form buys is brevity in one file. An input rule here stays one address to one name; grouping is what the DOCUMENT is for, and a binding that could group would be deciding logic in the dictionary.

unresolved.description: Written INSTEAD of `address`, when the platform's own list is not available yet and nobody has said which address this is. The string is the reason, for whoever can answer it. ⚠ This exists because absence has to be WRITABLE or it does not get written: a document is already platform-free -- it uses its own identifiers and the binding is the dictionary -- so the logic can be authored long before the addresses are known. Without a way to say 'not known yet', that gap gets filled with a plausible address instead, and a plausible wrong address is invisible. It is the peer of the document's `sce:unresolved`, which has stopped exactly this for VALUES since before this file existed.

not_equals.$comment: Kept distinct from equals_any on purpose: a negation stays correct when the enumeration grows, and a positive list silently narrows.

number.description: Pass the number itself rather than a truth value.

range.description: Admissible bounds for a number. A value outside them is out of range, which is a different fact from zero and must not be folded into it silently.

absent.description: True when the address is not reporting at all. Absence is not a value the address takes, so it never belongs in a value space.

when_absent.description: What a NUMBER reads as when its address is not reporting, or reports outside `range`. ⚠ Required for a numeric input whose address a case may not drive -- there is no safe silent answer. Folding absence into zero made seven cases on one corpus look as though the specification had been misread, when what had actually happened was that nothing was reporting. A symbol comparison needs no such declaration: an address that is not reporting is not any symbol, which is already the answer. Out of range counts as absent here because a reading the platform cannot represent is not a reading.

previous_of.description: The value another input had on the previous round, named by that input's own identifier. Prose writes transitions, and a transition needs the earlier value. ⚠ Reading one requires examples that declare themselves `ordered`; without an order there is no previous round to have differed from.

state_of.description: An output this same document produced on the previous round, named by that output's own identifier.

initial.description: What `previous_of` or `state_of` yields on the FIRST round, when there is no previous one. For `previous_of` it may be omitted, and then the first round reads the input's current value -- the assumption that nothing had changed before observation began, which is what edge detection means in practice. For `state_of` there is no current value to fall back on, so omitting it makes the first round a refusal rather than a guess: an output fed back before it has ever been produced is a number nobody computed.

variant_is.description: True when the case's `variant` is one of these. Its own key rather than an address for the same reason `clock` is: a variant is not a signal -- nothing drives it and it takes no value space. It is what a record means by being taken from one build rather than another.

clock.description: This input receives the case's `elapsed_ms` -- how long the situation had held when it was observed -- rather than a value read from an address. It is its own key rather than an address because time is a different CATEGORY from a signal: it has no address, no value space, and nothing drives it. Measured as the one thing a whole subject matter's bindings needed and the published vocabulary could not say.

protocol.description: A way of reading declared by the pack's conventions.

parameters.description: Addresses the protocol needs, by the parameter names the pack declared.

event.description: The event to send the machine when this rule fires. A statechart is not READ the way a pure computation is -- it is driven by events -- so an address alone cannot say what the machine should be told. ⚠ Naming an event is what makes a case DRIVE anything: without one, a run would replay every case against a machine nobody sent anything to, and the verdict would be about a run that never happened. ⚠⚠ Nothing else here is a second way of saying this. A value the machine READS -- a level a guard compares against -- is already said by `address` plus the rules beside it; what changes for a statechart is how the driver delivers it, and that is the kind's business rather than the dictionary's.

becomes.description: The value the address must take for `event` to be sent. Omitted, the event is sent whenever the case DROVE this address at all, whatever the value, which is what a record of an observation usually means. ⚠ Distinct from `equals` and not a spelling of it: `equals` asks what an address IS and answers every round, `becomes` asks what it CHANGED TO and answers once. A machine told the same news every round is not being driven, it is being repeated at.

output.x-sce-deliberately-absent: There is no key for reading a value back out of the DATAMODEL, and none for reading the active CONFIGURATION, though a statechart answers through both. Neither is missing vocabulary. `address` plus `map` already says which position a document value lands at and as what symbol; what a statechart changes is where the driver goes to fetch that value, and a binding that said so would be describing the document's internals in the dictionary. The configuration is a further step: a state is not an output at all, and binding one would make a verification break on a rename that left the behaviour alone.

unresolved.description: Written INSTEAD of `address`, when nobody has yet said which address this output reaches. The string is the reason. An unresolved OUTPUT is narrower than an unresolved input: the rest of the document still runs, and only the positions this one would have written go unchecked.

map.description: Document value to the symbol written at the address.

passthrough.description: Write the number the document computed, unmapped.

also.description: Other fields of the same address that always accompany this one.

when.description: Other fields that accompany a particular document value. Applied before `also`, so a default in `also` would overwrite these rather than fill the gaps.

internal.description: The document computes this and it reaches no address. Without it, a document's own carried state is never computed at all and every read of it returns a default, which looks like wrong logic rather than absent logic.

sent.description: This output leaves the document as a `<send>` to a host-served processor -- the W3C channel for reaching outside the machine (W3C SCXML 6.2), and the one a real platform receives. Without `param` or `content` the value IS the event name, so one rule covers every send that writes the same position and `map` turns each name into the symbol. ⚠ This is the channel to prefer, and that ordering is the key's whole point rather than a matter of taste: reading the datamodel or the configuration instead asserts against the document's insides, so splitting a state or renaming a variable breaks a verification whose subject did not change. What crossed the boundary is what a platform will see.

processor.description: The `type` written on the `<send>`, for a document served by more than one host processor where only one of them is this output. Omitted, any host-served send counts.

param.description: The `<param>` carrying this output's value. ⚠ `<param>` may repeat under one name and the runtime therefore delivers a LIST, so a rule naming a param that arrived more than once is a refusal: picking the first would be the driver deciding something the document said twice.

content.description: The send's `<content>` is this output's value.

when_nothing_sent.description: What this output reads as in a case where no matching send occurred. ⚠ REQUIRED beside `sent`, for the reason `when_absent` is required for a number: there is no safe silent answer. A machine that should have signalled and did not is the failure most worth catching, and an output that merely vanishes from the produced set is reported as a position nobody looked at -- which a reader takes for a clean run.
